displayDescription: A blue-hour toon-shaded miniature: an idea tower rises and lights a network of roads, houses and flow pods.
styleRenderer: Three.js 0.186.1 WebGLRenderer (procedural geometry, bundled locally with esbuild into diorama.js)
Quantized Toon Shading (MeshToonMaterial + 3-step NearestFilter DataTexture gradientMap)
Geometry Outlines and Crease Edges (EdgesGeometry → LineSegments2/LineMaterial crease lines; inverted-hull silhouettes on curved parts)
Soft Surface Lighting and Material Detail (hemisphere fill + soft PCF shadowed key light, contact-shadow catcher, translucent MeshPhysicalMaterial glass halo)
Video-Textured Screens and CRT Overlays (CanvasTexture tower screen redrawn from timeline progress with deterministic scanlines)
motionEngine: GSAP 3 paused timeline (sole owner of every scene-state property)
Scene Assembly and Part Animation (procedural named Object3D parts with keyed scale/position states; glTF-style part workflow, no glTF files loaded)
Camera Navigation (deterministic authored orbit + push-in path; no live controls or raycast input)
audioDescription: Silent. No audio track, music, effects or voiceover.
limitations: Blender, bpy, Cycles and EEVEE were not used, per the user's instruction; the diorama is a real-time Three.js approximation of an offline render.
Illustrative procedural scene: materials are toon-shaded flat colours, not physically measured; the glass halo is a transparent standard-physical material approximation without true refraction.
No glTF assets are loaded; parts are procedurally assembled Object3D groups animated the way glTF parts would be.
Raycast interaction is interactive-only and is not used; camera navigation is an authored deterministic path.
The CRT screen is a CanvasTexture redrawn from time, not decoded video.
No depth of field is applied, so the subject stays sharp; depth is suggested by perspective, fog and shadows.
Tone mapping is disabled to keep approved material colours close to their values; toon lighting bands still shift displayed values.
Three.js library internals contain Math.random (UUIDs) and requestAnimationFrame helpers that this composition never uses for visual state.
Not rendered or browser-tested by the agent; host QA is pending.
